document_host.note: Same product as Bury's store, under a different app path. RunThirdPartySearch?FileSystemId=PL&FOLDER1_REF=<REF> returns a real page ('Documents for reference 26/0475: Public Access') with zero rows to a plain client: the rows arrive over a SignalR hub. Files would come from /PublicAccess_Live/Document/ViewDocument.

quirks.summary: The Idox register has no documents tab; documents are on a separate host running the same SignalR-driven store as Bury, so no plain client can enumerate them.
quirks.detail: Verified 2026-09-30. activeTab=externalDocuments links to documents.newport.gov.uk/PublicAccess_LIVE/SearchResult/RunThirdPartySearch?FileSystemId=PL&FOLDER1_REF=26/0475. That returns HTTP 200 and a real page with no document rows: the markup loads jquery.signalR-2.4.2, Views/SearchResult/Index.js and dataTables, and sets viewDocumentUrl = '/PublicAccess_Live/Document/ViewDocument'. Identical product to Bury's store.
quirks.workaround: Construct the store URL from the reference and hand it over; do not attempt the SignalR negotiation.

quirks.summary: Unlike Bury, FOLDER1_REF here is the planning reference itself (26/0475), not an internal id.
quirks.detail: So the document-store link can be built from the reference alone, without first scraping the externalDocuments tab.

quirks.summary: The store's app path is /PublicAccess_LIVE/ and the string 'AniteIM' appears nowhere, so path-based detection of this product fails here.
quirks.detail: Detect it on the script set and endpoint instead: Scripts/Common.js, dataTables.select.min.js, jquery.signalR-2.4.2.min.js, Views/SearchResult/Index.js, SearchResult/RunThirdPartySearch and a 'Documents for reference <n>' title.

robots.note: robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /' - a blanket disallow for all crawlers.

browser_route.note: FOLDER1_REF here is the human reference, so this link is constructible without scraping.
